modules.title: Anomaly cancellation conditions
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

Anomaly cancellation conditions (ACCs) are consistency conditions which arise
in gauge field theories. They correspond to a set of homogeneous diophantine equations
in the rational charges assigned to fermions under `u(1)` contributions to the gauge group.

These formally arise from triangle Feynman diagrams, but can otherwise be got from
index theorems.

## ii. Key results

There are four different types related to the underlying structure of
the ACCs:
- `ACCSystemCharges`: the structure carrying the number of charges present.
- `ACCSystemLinear`: the structure extending `ACCSystemCharges` with linear anomaly cancellation
  conditions.
- `ACCSystemQuad`: the structure extending `ACCSystemLinear` with quadratic anomaly cancellation
  conditions.
- `ACCSystem`: the structure extending `ACCSystemQuad` with the cubic anomaly cancellation
  condition.

Related to these are the different types of spaces of charges:
- `Charges`: the module of all possible charge allocations.
- `LinSols`: the module of solutions to the linear ACCs.
- `QuadSols`: the solutions to the linear and quadratic ACCs.
- `Sols`: the solutions to the full ACCs.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The module of charges
- B. The module of charges
  - B.1. The `ℚ`-module structure on the type `Charges`
  - B.2. The finiteness of the `ℚ`-module structure on `Charges`
- C. The linear anomaly cancellation conditions
- D. The module of solutions to the linear ACCs
  - D.1. Extensionality of solutions to the linear ACCs
  - D.2. Module structure on the solutions to the linear ACCs
  - D.3. Embedding of the solutions to the linear ACCs into the module of charges
- E. The quadratic anomaly cancellation conditions
- F. The solutions to the quadratic and linear anomaly cancellation conditions
  - F.1. Extensionality of solutions to the quadratic and linear ACCs
  - F.2. MulAction of rationals on the solutions to the quadratic and linear ACCs
  - F.3. Embeddings of quadratic solutions into linear solutions
  - F.4. Embeddings of solutions to linear ACCs into quadratic solutions when no quadratics
  - F.5. Embeddings of quadratic solutions into all charges
- G. The full anomaly cancellation conditions
- H. The solutions to the full anomaly cancellation conditions
  - H.1. Extensionality of solutions to the ACCs
  - H.2. The `IsSolution` predicate
  - H.3. MulAction of `ℚ` on the solutions to the ACCs
  - H.4. Embeddings of solutions to the ACCs into quadratic solutions
  - H.5. Embeddings of solutions to the ACCs into linear solutions
  - H.6. Embeddings of solutions to the ACCs into charges
- I. Morphisms between ACC systems
  - I.1. Composition of morphisms between ACC systems
- J. Open TODO items

## iv. References

* Alvarez-Gaume, L. and Ginsparg, P. H. (1985). The Structure of Gauge and Gravitational Anomalies.
  [ref: alvarez_gaume_ginsparg_1985]
* Bilal, A. (2008). Lectures on Anomalies. arXiv preprint. [ref: bilal_2008_anomalies]
* Nash, C. (1991). Differential topology and quantum field theory. Elsevier. [ref: nash_1991_dtqft]

sections.text:
## A. The module of charges

We define the type `ACCSystemCharges`, this carries the charges
of the specification of the number of charges present in a theory.

For example for the standard model without right-handed neutrinos, this is `15` charges,
whilst with right handed neutrinos it is `18` charges.

We can think of `Fin χ.numberCharges` as an indexing type for
the representations present in the theory where `χ : ACCSystemCharges`.

## B. The module of charges

Given an `ACCSystemCharges` object `χ`, we define the type of charges
`χ.Charges` as functions from `Fin χ.numberCharges → ℚ`.

That is, for each representation in the theory, indexed by an element of `Fin χ.numberCharges`,
we assign a rational charge.

### B.1. The `ℚ`-module structure on the type `Charges`

The type `χ.Charges` has the structure of a module over the field `ℚ`.

### B.2. The finiteness of the `ℚ`-module structure on `Charges`

The type `χ.Charges` is a finite module.

## C. The linear anomaly cancellation conditions

We define the type `ACCSystemLinear` which extends `ACCSystemCharges` by adding
a finite number (determined by `numberLinear`) of linear equations in the rational charges.

## D. The module of solutions to the linear ACCs

We define the type `LinSols` of solutions to the linear ACCs.
That is the submodule of `χ.Charges` which satisfy all the linear ACCs.

### D.1. Extensionality of solutions to the linear ACCs

We prove a lemma relating to the equality of two elements of `LinSols`.

### D.2. Module structure on the solutions to the linear ACCs

we now give a module structure to `LinSols`.

### D.3. Embedding of the solutions to the linear ACCs into the module of charges

We give the linear embedding of solutions to the linear ACCs `LinSols` into
the module of all `charges`.

## E. The quadratic anomaly cancellation conditions

We extend `ACCSystemLinear` to `ACCSystemQuad` by adding a finite number
(determined by `numberQuadratic`) of quadratic equations in the rational charges.

These quadratic anomaly cancellation conditions correspond to the interaction
of the `u(1)` part of the gauge group of interest with another abelian part.

## F. The solutions to the quadratic and linear anomaly cancellation conditions

We define the type `QuadSols` of solutions to the linear and quadratic ACCs.

### F.1. Extensionality of solutions to the quadratic and linear ACCs

We prove a lemma relating to the equality of two elements of `QuadSols`.

### F.2. MulAction of rationals on the solutions to the quadratic and linear ACCs

The type `QuadSols` does not carry the structure of a module over `ℚ` as
the quadratic ACCs are not linear. However it does carry the structure of
a `MulAction` of `ℚ`.

### F.3. Embeddings of quadratic solutions into linear solutions

We give the equivariant of solutions to the quadratic and linear ACCs `QuadSols` into
the solutions to the linear ACCs `LinSols`.

### F.4. Embeddings of solutions to linear ACCs into quadratic solutions when no quadratics

When there are no quadratic ACCs, the solutions to the linear ACCs embed into the solutions
to the quadratic and linear ACCs.

### F.5. Embeddings of quadratic solutions into all charges

We give the equivariant embedding of solutions to the quadratic and linear ACCs `QuadSols` into
the module of all charges `Charges`.

## G. The full anomaly cancellation conditions

We extend `ACCSystemQuad` to `ACCSystem` by adding the single cubic equation
in the rational charges. This corresponds to the `u(1)^3` anomaly.

## H. The solutions to the full anomaly cancellation conditions

We define the type `Sols` of solutions to the full ACCs.

### H.1. Extensionality of solutions to the ACCs

We prove a lemma relating to the equality of two elements of `Sols`.

### H.2. The `IsSolution` predicate

we define a predicate on charges which is true if they correspond to a solution.

### H.3. MulAction of `ℚ` on the solutions to the ACCs

Like with `QuadSols`, the type `Sols` does not carry the structure of a module over `ℚ`
as the cubic nor quadratic ACC is not linear. However it does carry the structure of
a `MulAction` of `ℚ`.
### H.4. Embeddings of solutions to the ACCs into quadratic solutions
### H.5. Embeddings of solutions to the ACCs into linear solutions
### H.6. Embeddings of solutions to the ACCs into charges

## I. Morphisms between ACC systems

We define a morphisms between two `ACCSystem` objects.
as a linear map between their spaces of charges and a map between their spaces of solutions
such that mapping solutions and then including in the module of charges
is the same as including in the module of charges and then mapping charges.
### I.1. Composition of morphisms between ACC systems

## J. Open TODO items

We give some open TODO items for future work.

One natural direction is to formalize how the anomaly cancellation conditions defining an
`ACCSystem` arise from gauge-theoretic data (a gauge group together with fermionic representations).
Physically these arise from triangle Feynman diagrams, and can also be described via index-theoretic
or characteristic-class constructions (e.g. through an anomaly polynomial). At present we do not
formalize this derivation in Lean, and instead take the resulting homogeneous forms as data.

(To view these you may need to go to the GitHub source code for the file.)

declarations.name: ACCSystemCharges
declarations.doc: A system of charges, specified by the number of charges.
declarations.statement:
structure ACCSystemCharges where
  /-- The number of charges. -/
  numberCharges : ℕ

declarations.name: ACCSystemCharges.Charges
declarations.doc: The charges as functions from `Fin χ.numberCharges → ℚ`.
declarations.statement: def Charges (χ : ACCSystemCharges) : Type

declarations.name: ACCSystemCharges.chargesAddCommMonoid
declarations.doc:
An instance to provide the necessary operations and properties for `charges` to form an additive
commutative monoid.
declarations.statement: instance chargesAddCommMonoid (χ : ACCSystemCharges) : AddCommMonoid χ.Charges

declarations.name: ACCSystemCharges.chargesModule
declarations.doc:
An instance to provide the necessary operations and properties for `charges` to form a module
over the field `ℚ`.
declarations.statement: instance chargesModule (χ : ACCSystemCharges) : Module ℚ χ.Charges

declarations.name: ACCSystemCharges.ChargesAddCommGroup
declarations.statement: instance ChargesAddCommGroup (χ : ACCSystemCharges) : AddCommGroup χ.Charges

declarations.doc: The module `χ.Charges` over `ℚ` is finite.
declarations.statement: instance (χ : ACCSystemCharges) : Module.Finite ℚ χ.Charges

declarations.name: ACCSystemLinear
declarations.doc: The type of charges plus the linear ACCs.
declarations.statement:
structure ACCSystemLinear extends ACCSystemCharges where
  /-- The number of linear ACCs. -/
  numberLinear : ℕ
  /-- The linear ACCs. -/
  linearACCs : Fin numberLinear → (toACCSystemCharges.Charges →ₗ[ℚ] ℚ)

declarations.name: ACCSystemLinear.LinSols
declarations.doc: The type of solutions to the linear ACCs.
declarations.statement:
structure LinSols (χ : ACCSystemLinear) where
  /-- The underlying charge. -/
  val : χ.1.Charges
  /-- The condition that the charge satisfies the linear ACCs. -/
  linearSol : ∀ i : Fin χ.numberLinear, χ.linearACCs i val = 0

declarations.name: ACCSystemLinear.LinSols.ext
declarations.doc: Two solutions are equal if the underlying charges are equal.
declarations.statement: lemma LinSols.ext {χ : ACCSystemLinear} {S T : χ.LinSols} (h : S.val = T.val) : S = T

declarations.name: ACCSystemLinear.linSolsAddCommMonoid
declarations.doc:
An instance providing the operations and properties for `LinSols` to form an
additive commutative monoid.
declarations.statement:
instance linSolsAddCommMonoid (χ : ACCSystemLinear) :
    AddCommMonoid χ.LinSols

declarations.name: ACCSystemLinear.linSolsModule
declarations.doc:
An instance providing the operations and properties for `LinSols` to form a
module over `ℚ`.
declarations.statement: instance linSolsModule (χ : ACCSystemLinear) : Module ℚ χ.LinSols

declarations.name: ACCSystemLinear.linSolsAddCommGroup
declarations.statement: instance linSolsAddCommGroup (χ : ACCSystemLinear) : AddCommGroup χ.LinSols

declarations.name: ACCSystemLinear.linSolsIncl
declarations.doc: The inclusion of `LinSols` into `charges`.
declarations.statement: def linSolsIncl (χ : ACCSystemLinear) : χ.LinSols →ₗ[ℚ] χ.Charges

declarations.name: ACCSystemLinear.linSolsIncl_injective
declarations.statement:
lemma linSolsIncl_injective (χ : ACCSystemLinear) :
    Function.Injective χ.linSolsIncl

declarations.name: ACCSystemQuad
declarations.doc: The type of charges plus the linear ACCs plus the quadratic ACCs.
declarations.statement:
structure ACCSystemQuad extends ACCSystemLinear where
  /-- The number of quadratic ACCs. -/
  numberQuadratic : ℕ
  /-- The quadratic ACCs. -/
  quadraticACCs : Fin numberQuadratic → HomogeneousQuadratic toACCSystemCharges.Charges

declarations.name: ACCSystemQuad.QuadSols
declarations.doc: The type of solutions to the linear and quadratic ACCs.
declarations.statement:
structure QuadSols (χ : ACCSystemQuad) extends χ.LinSols where
  /-- The condition that the charge satisfies the quadratic ACCs. -/
  quadSol : ∀ i : Fin χ.numberQuadratic, (χ.quadraticACCs i) val = 0

declarations.name: ACCSystemQuad.QuadSols.ext
declarations.doc: Two `QuadSols` are equal if the underlying charges are equal.
declarations.statement:
lemma QuadSols.ext {χ : ACCSystemQuad} {S T : χ.QuadSols} (h : S.val = T.val) :
    S = T

declarations.name: ACCSystemQuad.quadSolsMulAction
declarations.doc: An instance giving the properties and structures to define an action of `ℚ` on `QuadSols`.
declarations.statement: instance quadSolsMulAction (χ : ACCSystemQuad) : MulAction ℚ χ.QuadSols

declarations.name: ACCSystemQuad.quadSolsInclLinSols
declarations.doc: The inclusion of quadratic solutions into linear solutions.
declarations.statement: def quadSolsInclLinSols (χ : ACCSystemQuad) : χ.QuadSols →[ℚ] χ.LinSols

declarations.name: ACCSystemQuad.quadSolsInclLinSols_injective
declarations.statement:
lemma quadSolsInclLinSols_injective (χ : ACCSystemQuad) :
    Function.Injective χ.quadSolsInclLinSols

declarations.name: ACCSystemQuad.linSolsInclQuadSolsZero
declarations.doc:
The inclusion of the linear solutions into the quadratic solutions, where there is
no quadratic equations (i.e. no U(1)'s in the underlying gauge group).
declarations.statement:
def linSolsInclQuadSolsZero (χ : ACCSystemQuad) (h : χ.numberQuadratic = 0) :
    χ.LinSols →[ℚ] χ.QuadSols

declarations.name: ACCSystemQuad.quadSolsIncl
declarations.doc: The inclusion of quadratic solutions into all charges.
declarations.statement: def quadSolsIncl (χ : ACCSystemQuad) : χ.QuadSols →[ℚ] χ.Charges

declarations.name: ACCSystemQuad.quadSolsIncl_injective
declarations.statement:
lemma quadSolsIncl_injective (χ : ACCSystemQuad) :
    Function.Injective χ.quadSolsIncl

declarations.name: ACCSystem
declarations.doc:
The type of charges plus the anomaly cancellation conditions.

In many physical settings these conditions are derived formally from the gauge group and the
fermionic representations. They arise from triangle Feynman diagrams, and can also be obtained
using index-theoretic or characteristic-class constructions.

In this file, we take the resulting conditions as input data: linear, quadratic and cubic
homogeneous forms on the space of rational charges.
declarations.statement:
structure ACCSystem extends ACCSystemQuad where
  /-- The cubic ACC. -/
  cubicACC : HomogeneousCubic toACCSystemCharges.Charges

declarations.name: ACCSystem.Sols
declarations.doc: The type of solutions to the anomaly cancellation conditions.
declarations.statement:
structure Sols (χ : ACCSystem) extends χ.QuadSols where
  /-- The condition that the charge satisfies the cubic ACC. -/
  cubicSol : χ.cubicACC val = 0

declarations.name: ACCSystem.Sols.ext
declarations.doc: Two solutions are equal if the underlying charges are equal.
declarations.statement:
lemma Sols.ext {χ : ACCSystem} {S T : χ.Sols} (h : S.val = T.val) :
    S = T

declarations.name: ACCSystem.IsSolution
declarations.doc: A charge `S` is a solution if it extends to a solution.
declarations.statement: def IsSolution (χ : ACCSystem) (S : χ.Charges) : Prop

declarations.name: ACCSystem.solsMulAction
declarations.doc: An instance giving the properties and structures to define an action of `ℚ` on `Sols`.
declarations.statement: instance solsMulAction (χ : ACCSystem) : MulAction ℚ χ.Sols

declarations.name: ACCSystem.solsInclQuadSols
declarations.doc: The inclusion of `Sols` into `QuadSols`.
declarations.statement: def solsInclQuadSols (χ : ACCSystem) : χ.Sols →[ℚ] χ.QuadSols

declarations.name: ACCSystem.solsInclQuadSols_injective
declarations.statement:
lemma solsInclQuadSols_injective (χ : ACCSystem) :
    Function.Injective χ.solsInclQuadSols

declarations.name: ACCSystem.solsInclLinSols
declarations.doc: The inclusion of `Sols` into `LinSols`.
declarations.statement: def solsInclLinSols (χ : ACCSystem) : χ.Sols →[ℚ] χ.LinSols

declarations.name: ACCSystem.solsInclLinSols_injective
declarations.statement:
lemma solsInclLinSols_injective (χ : ACCSystem) :
    Function.Injective χ.solsInclLinSols

declarations.name: ACCSystem.solsIncl
declarations.doc: The inclusion of `Sols` into `LinSols`.
declarations.statement: def solsIncl (χ : ACCSystem) : χ.Sols →[ℚ] χ.Charges

declarations.name: ACCSystem.solsIncl_injective
declarations.statement:
lemma solsIncl_injective (χ : ACCSystem) :
    Function.Injective χ.solsIncl

declarations.name: ACCSystem.Hom
declarations.doc: The structure of a map between two ACCSystems.
declarations.statement:
structure Hom (χ η : ACCSystem) where
  /-- The linear map between vector spaces of charges. -/
  charges : χ.Charges →ₗ[ℚ] η.Charges
  /-- The map between solutions. -/
  anomalyFree : χ.Sols → η.Sols
  /-- The condition that the map commutes with the relevant inclusions. -/
  commute : charges ∘ χ.solsIncl = η.solsIncl ∘ anomalyFree

declarations.name: ACCSystem.Hom.comp
declarations.doc: The definition of composition between two ACCSystems.
declarations.statement: def Hom.comp {χ η ε : ACCSystem} (g : Hom η ε) (f : Hom χ η) : Hom χ ε

modules.title: Group actions on ACC systems.
modules.doc:
We define a group action on an ACC system as a representation on the vector spaces of charges
under which the anomaly equations are invariant.

From this we define
- The representation acting on the vector space of solutions to the linear ACCs.
- The group action acting on solutions to the linear + quadratic equations.
- The group action acting on solutions to the anomaly cancellation conditions.

declarations.name: ACCSystemGroupAction
declarations.doc:
The type of a group action on a system of charges is defined as a representation on
the vector spaces of charges under which the anomaly equations are invariant.
declarations.statement:
structure ACCSystemGroupAction (χ : ACCSystem) where
  /-- The underlying type of the group. -/
  group : Type
  /-- An instance given the `group` component the structure of a `Group`. -/
  groupInst : Group group
  /-- The representation of group acting on the vector space of charges. -/
  rep : Representation ℚ group χ.Charges
  /-- The invariance of the linear ACCs under the group action. -/
  linearInvariant : ∀ i g S, χ.linearACCs i (rep g S) = χ.linearACCs i S
  /-- The invariance of the quadratic ACCs under the group action. -/
  quadInvariant : ∀ i g S, (χ.quadraticACCs i) (rep g S) = (χ.quadraticACCs i) S
  /-- The invariance of the cubic ACC under the group action. -/
  cubicInvariant : ∀ g S, χ.cubicACC (rep g S) = χ.cubicACC S

declarations.doc: The given instance of a group on the `group` field of a `ACCSystemGroupAction`.
declarations.statement: instance {χ : ACCSystem} (G : ACCSystemGroupAction χ) : Group G.group

declarations.name: ACCSystemGroupAction.linSolMap
declarations.doc: The action of a group element on the vector space of linear solutions.
declarations.statement:
def linSolMap {χ : ACCSystem} (G : ACCSystemGroupAction χ) (g : G.group) :
    χ.LinSols →ₗ[ℚ] χ.LinSols

declarations.name: ACCSystemGroupAction.linSolRep
declarations.doc: The representation acting on the vector space of solutions to the linear ACCs.
declarations.statement:
def linSolRep {χ : ACCSystem} (G : ACCSystemGroupAction χ) :
    Representation ℚ G.group χ.LinSols

declarations.name: ACCSystemGroupAction.rep_linSolRep_commute
declarations.doc:
The representation on the charges and anomaly free solutions
commutes with the inclusion.
declarations.statement:
lemma rep_linSolRep_commute {χ : ACCSystem} (G : ACCSystemGroupAction χ) (g : G.group)
    (S : χ.LinSols) : χ.linSolsIncl (G.linSolRep g S) =
    G.rep g (χ.linSolsIncl S)

declarations.name: ACCSystemGroupAction.quadSolAction
declarations.doc: A multiplicative action of `G.group` on `quadSols`.
declarations.statement:
instance quadSolAction {χ : ACCSystem} (G : ACCSystemGroupAction χ) :
    MulAction G.group χ.QuadSols

declarations.name: ACCSystemGroupAction.linSolRep_quadSolAction_commute
declarations.statement:
lemma linSolRep_quadSolAction_commute {χ : ACCSystem} (G : ACCSystemGroupAction χ) (g : G.group)
    (S : χ.QuadSols) : χ.quadSolsInclLinSols (G.quadSolAction.toFun _ _ S g) =
    G.linSolRep g (χ.quadSolsInclLinSols S)

declarations.name: ACCSystemGroupAction.rep_quadSolAction_commute
declarations.statement:
lemma rep_quadSolAction_commute {χ : ACCSystem} (G : ACCSystemGroupAction χ) (g : G.group)
    (S : χ.QuadSols) : χ.quadSolsIncl (G.quadSolAction.toFun _ _ S g) =
    G.rep g (χ.quadSolsIncl S)

declarations.name: ACCSystemGroupAction.solAction
declarations.doc: The group action acting on solutions to the anomaly cancellation conditions.
declarations.statement: instance solAction {χ : ACCSystem} (G : ACCSystemGroupAction χ) : MulAction G.group χ.Sols

declarations.name: ACCSystemGroupAction.quadSolAction_solAction_commute
declarations.statement:
lemma quadSolAction_solAction_commute {χ : ACCSystem} (G : ACCSystemGroupAction χ) (g : G.group)
    (S : χ.Sols) : χ.solsInclQuadSols (G.solAction.toFun _ _ S g) =
    G.quadSolAction.toFun _ _ (χ.solsInclQuadSols S) g

declarations.name: ACCSystemGroupAction.linSolRep_solAction_commute
declarations.statement:
lemma linSolRep_solAction_commute {χ : ACCSystem} (G : ACCSystemGroupAction χ) (g : G.group)
    (S : χ.Sols) : χ.solsInclLinSols (G.solAction.toFun _ _ S g) =
    G.linSolRep g (χ.solsInclLinSols S)

declarations.name: ACCSystemGroupAction.rep_solAction_commute
declarations.statement:
lemma rep_solAction_commute {χ : ACCSystem} (G : ACCSystemGroupAction χ) (g : G.group)
    (S : χ.Sols) : χ.solsIncl (G.solAction.toFun _ _ S g) = G.rep g (χ.solsIncl S)

modules.title: Creation and annihilation parts of fields

declarations.name: CreateAnnihilate
declarations.doc:
The type `CreateAnnihilate` is the type containing two elements `create` and `annihilate`.
This type is used to specify if an operator is a creation, or annihilation, operator
or the sum thereof or integral thereof etc.
declarations.statement:
inductive CreateAnnihilate where
  | create : CreateAnnihilate
  | annihilate : CreateAnnihilate
deriving Inhabited, BEq, DecidableEq

declarations.doc: The type `CreateAnnihilate` is finite.
declarations.statement: instance : Fintype CreateAnnihilate

declarations.name: CreateAnnihilate.eq_create_or_annihilate
declarations.statement: lemma eq_create_or_annihilate (φ : CreateAnnihilate) : φ = create ∨ φ = annihilate

declarations.name: CreateAnnihilate.normalOrder
declarations.doc:
The normal ordering on creation and annihilation operators.
Under this relation, `normalOrder a b` is false only if `a` is annihilate and `b` is create.
declarations.statement: def normalOrder : CreateAnnihilate → CreateAnnihilate → Prop

declarations.doc: The normal ordering on `CreateAnnihilate` is decidable.
declarations.statement: instance : (φ φ' : CreateAnnihilate) → Decidable (normalOrder φ φ')

declarations.doc: Normal ordering is total.
declarations.statement: instance : Std.Total normalOrder

declarations.doc: Normal ordering is transitive.
declarations.statement: instance : IsTrans CreateAnnihilate normalOrder

declarations.name: CreateAnnihilate.not_normalOrder_annihilate_iff_false
declarations.statement:
lemma not_normalOrder_annihilate_iff_false (a : CreateAnnihilate) :
    (¬ normalOrder a annihilate) ↔ False

declarations.name: CreateAnnihilate.sum_eq
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_eq {M : Type} [AddCommMonoid M] (f : CreateAnnihilate → M) :
    ∑ i, f i = f create + f annihilate

declarations.name: CreateAnnihilate.CreateAnnihilate_card_eq_two
declarations.statement: lemma CreateAnnihilate_card_eq_two : Fintype.card CreateAnnihilate = 2

modules.title: Feynman diagrams
modules.doc:
Feynman diagrams form a type into which permissible Wick contractions
embed.

A permissible Wick contraction is one which does not contribute zero to
the vacuum expectation value.

Feynman diagrams are based on multisets of `FieldOp`. This should be contrasted
with Wick contractions which are based on lists of `FieldOp`.

In particular a Feynman diagram is a partition of a Multiset into
disjoint pairs.

## Note

This directory is currently a work in progress.
(Contact JTS before working in this directory.)

modules.title: Creation and annihilation free-algebra
modules.doc:
This module defines the creation and annihilation algebra for a field structure.

The creation and annihilation algebra extends from the state algebra by adding information about
whether a state is a creation or annihilation operator.

The algebra is spanned by lists of creation/annihilation states.

The main structures defined in this module are:

* `FieldOpFreeAlgebra` - The creation and annihilation algebra
* `ofCrAnOpF` - Maps a creation/annihilation state to the algebra
* `ofCrAnListF` - Maps a list of creation/annihilation states to the algebra
* `ofFieldOpF` - Maps a state to a sum of creation and annihilation operators
* `crPartF` - The creation part of a state in the algebra
* `anPartF` - The annihilation part of a state in the algebra
* `superCommuteF` - The super commutator on the algebra

The key lemmas show how these operators interact, particularly focusing on the
super commutation relations between creation and annihilation operators.

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra
declarations.doc:
For a field specification `𝓕`, the algebra `𝓕.FieldOpFreeAlgebra` is
the free algebra generated by `𝓕.CrAnFieldOp`.
declarations.statement: abbrev FieldOpFreeAlgebra (𝓕 : FieldSpecification) : Type

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.ofCrAnOpF
declarations.doc:
For a field specification `𝓕`, and a element `φ` of `𝓕.CrAnFieldOp`,
`ofCrAnOpF φ` is defined as the element of `𝓕.FieldOpFreeAlgebra` formed by `φ`.
declarations.statement: def ofCrAnOpF (φ : 𝓕.CrAnFieldOp) : FieldOpFreeAlgebra 𝓕

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.universality
declarations.doc:
The algebra `𝓕.FieldOpFreeAlgebra` satisfies the universal property that for any other algebra
  `A` (e.g. the operator algebra of the theory) with a map `f : 𝓕.CrAnFieldOp → A` (e.g.
  the inclusion of the creation and annihilation parts of field operators into the
  operator algebra) there is a unique algebra map `g : 𝓕.FieldOpFreeAlgebra → A`
  such that `g ∘ ofCrAnOpF = f`.

  The unique `g` is given by `FreeAlgebra.lift ℂ f`.
declarations.statement:
lemma universality {A : Type} [Semiring A] [Algebra ℂ A] (f : 𝓕.CrAnFieldOp → A) :
    ∃! g : FieldOpFreeAlgebra 𝓕 →ₐ[ℂ] A, g ∘ ofCrAnOpF = f

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.ofCrAnListF
declarations.doc:
For a field specification `𝓕`, and a list `φs` of `𝓕.CrAnFieldOp`,
`ofCrAnListF φs` is defined as the element of `𝓕.FieldOpFreeAlgebra`
obtained by the product of `ofCrAnListF φ` for each `φ` in `φs`.
For example `ofCrAnListF [φ₁, φ₂, φ₃] = ofCrAnOpF φ₁ * ofCrAnOpF φ₂ * ofCrAnOpF φ₃`.
The set of all `ofCrAnListF φs` forms a basis of `FieldOpFreeAlgebra 𝓕`.
declarations.statement: def ofCrAnListF (φs : List 𝓕.CrAnFieldOp) : FieldOpFreeAlgebra 𝓕

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.ofCrAnListF_nil
declarations.statement: lemma ofCrAnListF_nil : ofCrAnListF ([] : List 𝓕.CrAnFieldOp) = 1

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.ofCrAnListF_cons
declarations.statement:
lemma ofCrAnListF_cons (φ : 𝓕.CrAnFieldOp) (φs : List 𝓕.CrAnFieldOp) :
    ofCrAnListF (φ :: φs) = ofCrAnOpF φ * ofCrAnListF φs

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.ofCrAnListF_append
declarations.statement:
lemma ofCrAnListF_append (φs φs' : List 𝓕.CrAnFieldOp) :
    ofCrAnListF (φs ++ φs') = ofCrAnListF φs * ofCrAnListF φs'

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.ofCrAnListF_singleton
declarations.statement:
lemma ofCrAnListF_singleton (φ : 𝓕.CrAnFieldOp) :
    ofCrAnListF [φ] = ofCrAnOpF φ

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.ofFieldOpF
declarations.doc:
For a field specification `𝓕`, and an element `φ` of `𝓕.FieldOp`,
`ofFieldOpF φ` is the element of `𝓕.FieldOpFreeAlgebra` formed by summing over
`ofCrAnOpF` of the
creation and annihilation parts of `φ`.

For example, for `φ` an incoming asymptotic field operator we get
`ofCrAnOpF ⟨φ, ()⟩`, and for `φ` a
position field operator we get `ofCrAnOpF ⟨φ, .create⟩ + ofCrAnOpF ⟨φ, .annihilate⟩`.
declarations.statement: def ofFieldOpF (φ : 𝓕.FieldOp) : FieldOpFreeAlgebra 𝓕

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.ofFieldOpListF
declarations.doc:
For a field specification `𝓕`, and a list `φs` of `𝓕.FieldOp`,
`𝓕.ofFieldOpListF φs` is defined as the element of `𝓕.FieldOpFreeAlgebra`
obtained by the product of `ofFieldOpF φ` for each `φ` in `φs`.
For example `ofFieldOpListF [φ₁, φ₂, φ₃] = ofFieldOpF φ₁ * ofFieldOpF φ₂ * ofFieldOpF φ₃`.
declarations.statement: def ofFieldOpListF (φs : List 𝓕.FieldOp) : FieldOpFreeAlgebra 𝓕

declarations.doc: Coercion from `List 𝓕.FieldOp` to `FieldOpFreeAlgebra 𝓕` through `ofFieldOpListF`.
declarations.statement: instance : Coe (List 𝓕.FieldOp) (FieldOpFreeAlgebra 𝓕)

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.ofFieldOpListF_nil
declarations.statement: lemma ofFieldOpListF_nil : ofFieldOpListF ([] : List 𝓕.FieldOp) = 1

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.ofFieldOpListF_cons
declarations.statement:
lemma ofFieldOpListF_cons (φ : 𝓕.FieldOp) (φs : List 𝓕.FieldOp) :
    ofFieldOpListF (φ :: φs) = ofFieldOpF φ * ofFieldOpListF φs

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.ofFieldOpListF_singleton
declarations.statement:
lemma ofFieldOpListF_singleton (φ : 𝓕.FieldOp) :
    ofFieldOpListF [φ] = ofFieldOpF φ

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.ofFieldOpListF_append
declarations.statement:
lemma ofFieldOpListF_append (φs φs' : List 𝓕.FieldOp) :
    ofFieldOpListF (φs ++ φs') = ofFieldOpListF φs * ofFieldOpListF φs'

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.ofFieldOpListF_sum
declarations.statement:
lemma ofFieldOpListF_sum (φs : List 𝓕.FieldOp) :
    ofFieldOpListF φs = ∑ (s : CrAnSection φs), ofCrAnListF s.1

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.crPartF
declarations.doc:
The algebra map taking an element of the free-state algebra to
the part of it in the creation and annihilation free algebra
spanned by creation operators.
declarations.statement: def crPartF : 𝓕.FieldOp → 𝓕.FieldOpFreeAlgebra

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.crPartF_negAsymp
declarations.statement:
lemma crPartF_negAsymp (φ : (Σ f, 𝓕.AsymptoticLabel f) × Momentum) :
    crPartF (FieldOp.inAsymp φ) = ofCrAnOpF ⟨FieldOp.inAsymp φ, ()⟩

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.crPartF_position
declarations.statement:
lemma crPartF_position (φ : (Σ f, 𝓕.PositionLabel f) × SpaceTime) :
    crPartF (FieldOp.position φ) =
    ofCrAnOpF ⟨FieldOp.position φ, CreateAnnihilate.create⟩

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.crPartF_posAsymp
declarations.statement:
lemma crPartF_posAsymp (φ : (Σ f, 𝓕.AsymptoticLabel f) × Momentum) :
    crPartF (FieldOp.outAsymp φ) = 0

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.anPartF
declarations.doc:
The algebra map taking an element of the free-state algebra to
the part of it in the creation and annihilation free algebra
spanned by annihilation operators.
declarations.statement: def anPartF : 𝓕.FieldOp → 𝓕.FieldOpFreeAlgebra

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.anPartF_negAsymp
declarations.statement:
lemma anPartF_negAsymp (φ : (Σ f, 𝓕.AsymptoticLabel f) × Momentum) :
    anPartF (FieldOp.inAsymp φ) = 0

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.anPartF_position
declarations.statement:
lemma anPartF_position (φ : (Σ f, 𝓕.PositionLabel f) × SpaceTime) :
    anPartF (FieldOp.position φ) =
    ofCrAnOpF ⟨FieldOp.position φ, CreateAnnihilate.annihilate⟩

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.anPartF_posAsymp
declarations.statement:
lemma anPartF_posAsymp (φ : (Σ f, 𝓕.AsymptoticLabel f) × Momentum) :
    anPartF (FieldOp.outAsymp φ) = ofCrAnOpF ⟨FieldOp.outAsymp φ, ()⟩

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.ofFieldOpF_eq_crPartF_add_anPartF
declarations.statement:
lemma ofFieldOpF_eq_crPartF_add_anPartF (φ : 𝓕.FieldOp) :
    ofFieldOpF φ = crPartF φ + anPartF φ

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.ofCrAnListFBasis
declarations.doc: The basis of the free creation and annihilation algebra formed by lists of CrAnFieldOp.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def ofCrAnListFBasis : Basis (List 𝓕.CrAnFieldOp) ℂ (FieldOpFreeAlgebra 𝓕)

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.ofListBasis_eq_ofList
declarations.statement:
lemma ofListBasis_eq_ofList (φs : List 𝓕.CrAnFieldOp) :
    ofCrAnListFBasis φs = ofCrAnListF φs

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.ofCrAnListF_injective
declarations.statement: lemma ofCrAnListF_injective : Function.Injective (ofCrAnListF (𝓕 := 𝓕))

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.mulLinearMap
declarations.doc: The bi-linear map associated with multiplication in `FieldOpFreeAlgebra`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def mulLinearMap : FieldOpFreeAlgebra 𝓕 →ₗ[ℂ] FieldOpFreeAlgebra 𝓕 →ₗ[ℂ]
    FieldOpFreeAlgebra 𝓕

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.mulLinearMap_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma mulLinearMap_apply (a b : FieldOpFreeAlgebra 𝓕) :
    mulLinearMap a b = a * b

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.smulLinearMap
declarations.doc: The linear map associated with scalar-multiplication in `FieldOpFreeAlgebra`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def smulLinearMap (c : ℂ) : FieldOpFreeAlgebra 𝓕 →ₗ[ℂ] FieldOpFreeAlgebra 𝓕

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.statisticSubmodule
declarations.doc: The submodule of `FieldOpFreeAlgebra` spanned by lists of field statistic `f`.
declarations.statement: def statisticSubmodule (f : FieldStatistic) : Submodule ℂ 𝓕.FieldOpFreeAlgebra

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.ofCrAnListF_mem_statisticSubmodule_of
declarations.statement:
lemma ofCrAnListF_mem_statisticSubmodule_of (φs : List 𝓕.CrAnFieldOp) (f : FieldStatistic)
    (h : (𝓕 |>ₛ φs) = f) :
    ofCrAnListF φs ∈ statisticSubmodule f

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.ofCrAnListF_bosonic_or_fermionic
declarations.statement:
lemma ofCrAnListF_bosonic_or_fermionic (φs : List 𝓕.CrAnFieldOp) :
    ofCrAnListF φs ∈ statisticSubmodule bosonic ∨
    ofCrAnListF φs ∈ statisticSubmodule fermionic

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.ofCrAnOpF_bosonic_or_fermionic
declarations.statement:
lemma ofCrAnOpF_bosonic_or_fermionic (φ : 𝓕.CrAnFieldOp) :
    ofCrAnOpF φ ∈ statisticSubmodule bosonic ∨ ofCrAnOpF φ ∈ statisticSubmodule fermionic

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.bosonicProjF
declarations.doc: The projection of an element of `FieldOpFreeAlgebra` onto it's bosonic part.
declarations.statement: def bosonicProjF : 𝓕.FieldOpFreeAlgebra →ₗ[ℂ] statisticSubmodule (𝓕 := 𝓕) bosonic

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.bosonicProjF_ofCrAnListF
declarations.statement:
lemma bosonicProjF_ofCrAnListF (φs : List 𝓕.CrAnFieldOp) :
    bosonicProjF (ofCrAnListF φs) = if h : (𝓕 |>ₛ φs) = bosonic then
      ⟨ofCrAnListF φs, Submodule.mem_span.mpr fun _ a => a ⟨φs, ⟨rfl, h⟩⟩⟩ else 0

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.bosonicProjF_of_mem_bosonic
declarations.statement:
lemma bosonicProjF_of_mem_bosonic (a : 𝓕.FieldOpFreeAlgebra) (h : a ∈ statisticSubmodule bosonic) :
    bosonicProjF a = ⟨a, h⟩

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.bosonicProjF_of_mem_fermionic
declarations.statement:
lemma bosonicProjF_of_mem_fermionic (a : 𝓕.FieldOpFreeAlgebra)
    (h : a ∈ statisticSubmodule fermionic) :
    bosonicProjF a = 0

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.bosonicProjF_of_bonosic_part
declarations.statement:
lemma bosonicProjF_of_bonosic_part
    (a : DirectSum FieldStatistic (fun i => (statisticSubmodule (𝓕 := 𝓕) i))) :
    bosonicProjF (a bosonic) = a bosonic

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.bosonicProjF_of_fermionic_part
declarations.statement:
lemma bosonicProjF_of_fermionic_part
    (a : DirectSum FieldStatistic (fun i => (statisticSubmodule (𝓕 := 𝓕) i))) :
    bosonicProjF (a fermionic).1 = 0

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.fermionicProjF
declarations.doc: The projection of an element of `FieldOpFreeAlgebra` onto it's fermionic part.
declarations.statement: def fermionicProjF : 𝓕.FieldOpFreeAlgebra →ₗ[ℂ] statisticSubmodule (𝓕 := 𝓕) fermionic

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.fermionicProjF_ofCrAnListF
declarations.statement:
lemma fermionicProjF_ofCrAnListF (φs : List 𝓕.CrAnFieldOp) :
    fermionicProjF (ofCrAnListF φs) = if h : (𝓕 |>ₛ φs) = fermionic then
      ⟨ofCrAnListF φs, Submodule.mem_span.mpr fun _ a => a ⟨φs, ⟨rfl, h⟩⟩⟩ else 0

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.fermionicProjF_ofCrAnListF_if_bosonic
declarations.statement:
lemma fermionicProjF_ofCrAnListF_if_bosonic (φs : List 𝓕.CrAnFieldOp) :
    fermionicProjF (ofCrAnListF φs) = if h : (𝓕 |>ₛ φs) = bosonic then
      0 else ⟨ofCrAnListF φs, Submodule.mem_span.mpr fun _ a => a ⟨φs, ⟨rfl,
        by simpa using h⟩⟩⟩

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.fermionicProjF_of_mem_fermionic
declarations.statement:
lemma fermionicProjF_of_mem_fermionic (a : 𝓕.FieldOpFreeAlgebra)
    (h : a ∈ statisticSubmodule fermionic) :
    fermionicProjF a = ⟨a, h⟩

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.fermionicProjF_of_mem_bosonic
declarations.statement:
lemma fermionicProjF_of_mem_bosonic (a : 𝓕.FieldOpFreeAlgebra)
    (h : a ∈ statisticSubmodule bosonic) : fermionicProjF a = 0

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.fermionicProjF_of_bosonic_part
declarations.statement:
lemma fermionicProjF_of_bosonic_part
    (a : DirectSum FieldStatistic (fun i => (statisticSubmodule (𝓕 := 𝓕) i))) :
    fermionicProjF (a bosonic).1 = 0

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.fermionicProjF_of_fermionic_part
declarations.statement:
lemma fermionicProjF_of_fermionic_part
    (a : DirectSum FieldStatistic (fun i => (statisticSubmodule (𝓕 := 𝓕) i))) :
    fermionicProjF (a fermionic) = a fermionic

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.bosonicProjF_add_fermionicProjF
declarations.statement:
lemma bosonicProjF_add_fermionicProjF (a : 𝓕.FieldOpFreeAlgebra) :
    a.bosonicProjF + (a.fermionicProjF).1 = a

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.coeAddMonoidHom_apply_eq_bosonic_plus_fermionic
declarations.statement:
lemma coeAddMonoidHom_apply_eq_bosonic_plus_fermionic
    (a : DirectSum FieldStatistic (fun i => (statisticSubmodule (𝓕 := 𝓕) i))) :
    DirectSum.coeAddMonoidHom statisticSubmodule a = a.1 bosonic + a.1 fermionic

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.directSum_eq_bosonic_plus_fermionic
declarations.statement:
lemma directSum_eq_bosonic_plus_fermionic
    (a : DirectSum FieldStatistic (fun i => (statisticSubmodule (𝓕 := 𝓕) i))) :
    a = (DirectSum.of (fun i => ↥(statisticSubmodule i)) bosonic) (a bosonic) +
    (DirectSum.of (fun i => ↥(statisticSubmodule i)) fermionic) (a fermionic)

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.fieldOpFreeAlgebraGrade
declarations.doc:
For a field specification `𝓕`, the algebra `𝓕.FieldOpFreeAlgebra` is graded by `FieldStatistic`.
Those `ofCrAnListF φs` for which `φs` has an overall `bosonic` statistic
(i.e. `𝓕 |>ₛ φs = bosonic`) span `bosonic`
submodule, whilst those `ofCrAnListF φs` for which `φs` has an overall `fermionic` statistic
(i.e. `𝓕 |>ₛ φs = fermionic`) span
the `fermionic` submodule.
declarations.statement:
instance fieldOpFreeAlgebraGrade :
    GradedAlgebra (A := 𝓕.FieldOpFreeAlgebra) statisticSubmodule

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.eq_zero_of_bosonic_and_fermionic
declarations.statement:
lemma eq_zero_of_bosonic_and_fermionic {a : 𝓕.FieldOpFreeAlgebra}
    (hb : a ∈ statisticSubmodule bosonic) (hf : a ∈ statisticSubmodule fermionic) : a = 0

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.bosonicProjF_mul
declarations.statement:
lemma bosonicProjF_mul (a b : 𝓕.FieldOpFreeAlgebra) :
    (a * b).bosonicProjF.1 = a.bosonicProjF.1 * b.bosonicProjF.1
    + a.fermionicProjF.1 * b.fermionicProjF.1

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.fermionicProjF_mul
declarations.statement:
lemma fermionicProjF_mul (a b : 𝓕.FieldOpFreeAlgebra) :
    (a * b).fermionicProjF.1 = a.bosonicProjF.1 * b.fermionicProjF.1
    + a.fermionicProjF.1 * b.bosonicProjF.1

modules.title: Normal Ordering in the FieldOpFreeAlgebra
modules.doc:

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.normalOrderF
declarations.doc:
For a field specification `𝓕`, `normalOrderF` is the linear map

`FieldOpFreeAlgebra 𝓕 →ₗ[ℂ] FieldOpFreeAlgebra 𝓕`

defined by its action on the basis `ofCrAnListF φs`, taking `ofCrAnListF φs` to

`normalOrderSign φs • ofCrAnListF (normalOrderList φs)`.

That is, `normalOrderF` normal-orders the field operators and multiplies by the sign of the
normal order.

The notation `𝓝ᶠ(a)` is used for `normalOrderF a` for `a` an element of
`FieldOpFreeAlgebra 𝓕`.
declarations.statement: def normalOrderF : FieldOpFreeAlgebra 𝓕 →ₗ[ℂ] FieldOpFreeAlgebra 𝓕

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.normalOrderF_ofCrAnListF
declarations.statement:
lemma normalOrderF_ofCrAnListF (φs : List 𝓕.CrAnFieldOp) :
    𝓝ᶠ(ofCrAnListF φs) = normalOrderSign φs • ofCrAnListF (normalOrderList φs)

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.ofCrAnListF_eq_normalOrderF
declarations.statement:
lemma ofCrAnListF_eq_normalOrderF (φs : List 𝓕.CrAnFieldOp) :
    ofCrAnListF (normalOrderList φs) = normalOrderSign φs • 𝓝ᶠ(ofCrAnListF φs)

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.normalOrderF_one
declarations.statement: lemma normalOrderF_one : normalOrderF (𝓕 := 𝓕) 1 = 1

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.normalOrderF_normalOrderF_mid
declarations.statement:
lemma normalOrderF_normalOrderF_mid (a b c : 𝓕.FieldOpFreeAlgebra) :
    𝓝ᶠ(a * b * c) = 𝓝ᶠ(a * 𝓝ᶠ(b) * c)

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.normalOrderF_normalOrderF_right
declarations.statement:
lemma normalOrderF_normalOrderF_right (a b : 𝓕.FieldOpFreeAlgebra) :
    𝓝ᶠ(a * b) = 𝓝ᶠ(a * 𝓝ᶠ(b))

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.normalOrderF_normalOrderF_left
declarations.statement:
lemma normalOrderF_normalOrderF_left (a b : 𝓕.FieldOpFreeAlgebra) :
    𝓝ᶠ(a * b) = 𝓝ᶠ(𝓝ᶠ(a) * b)

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.normalOrderF_ofCrAnListF_cons_create
declarations.statement:
lemma normalOrderF_ofCrAnListF_cons_create (φ : 𝓕.CrAnFieldOp)
    (hφ : 𝓕 |>ᶜ φ = CreateAnnihilate.create) (φs : List 𝓕.CrAnFieldOp) :
    𝓝ᶠ(ofCrAnListF (φ :: φs)) = ofCrAnOpF φ * 𝓝ᶠ(ofCrAnListF φs)

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.normalOrderF_create_mul
declarations.statement:
lemma normalOrderF_create_mul (φ : 𝓕.CrAnFieldOp)
    (hφ : 𝓕 |>ᶜ φ = CreateAnnihilate.create) (a : FieldOpFreeAlgebra 𝓕) :
    𝓝ᶠ(ofCrAnOpF φ * a) = ofCrAnOpF φ * 𝓝ᶠ(a)

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.normalOrderF_ofCrAnListF_append_annihilate
declarations.statement:
lemma normalOrderF_ofCrAnListF_append_annihilate (φ : 𝓕.CrAnFieldOp)
    (hφ : 𝓕 |>ᶜ φ = CreateAnnihilate.annihilate) (φs : List 𝓕.CrAnFieldOp) :
    𝓝ᶠ(ofCrAnListF (φs ++ [φ])) = 𝓝ᶠ(ofCrAnListF φs) * ofCrAnOpF φ

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.normalOrderF_mul_annihilate
declarations.statement:
lemma normalOrderF_mul_annihilate (φ : 𝓕.CrAnFieldOp)
    (hφ : 𝓕 |>ᶜ φ = CreateAnnihilate.annihilate)
    (a : FieldOpFreeAlgebra 𝓕) : 𝓝ᶠ(a * ofCrAnOpF φ) = 𝓝ᶠ(a) * ofCrAnOpF φ

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.normalOrderF_crPartF_mul
declarations.statement:
lemma normalOrderF_crPartF_mul (φ : 𝓕.FieldOp) (a : FieldOpFreeAlgebra 𝓕) :
    𝓝ᶠ(crPartF φ * a) =
    crPartF φ * 𝓝ᶠ(a)

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.normalOrderF_mul_anPartF
declarations.statement:
lemma normalOrderF_mul_anPartF (φ : 𝓕.FieldOp) (a : FieldOpFreeAlgebra 𝓕) :
    𝓝ᶠ(a * anPartF φ) =
    𝓝ᶠ(a) * anPartF φ

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.normalOrderF_swap_create_annihilate_ofCrAnListF_ofCrAnListF
declarations.statement:
lemma normalOrderF_swap_create_annihilate_ofCrAnListF_ofCrAnListF (φc φa : 𝓕.CrAnFieldOp)

      normalOrderSign (φs ++ φc' :: φc :: φs') •
    (ofCrAnListF (createFilter φs) * [ofCrAnOpF φc, ofCrAnOpF φc']ₛF *
      ofCrAnListF (createFilter φs') * ofCrAnListF (annihilateFilter (φs ++ φs')))

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.superCommuteF
declarations.doc:
For a field specification `𝓕`, the super commutator `superCommuteF` is defined as the linear
map `𝓕.FieldOpFreeAlgebra →ₗ[ℂ] 𝓕.FieldOpFreeAlgebra →ₗ[ℂ] 𝓕.FieldOpFreeAlgebra`
which on the lists `φs` and `φs'` of `𝓕.CrAnFieldOp` gives

`superCommuteF φs φs' = φs * φs' - 𝓢(φs, φs') • φs' * φs`.

The notation `[a, b]ₛF` can be used for `superCommuteF a b`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def superCommuteF : 𝓕.FieldOpFreeAlgebra →ₗ[ℂ] 𝓕.FieldOpFreeAlgebra →ₗ[ℂ]
    𝓕.FieldOpFreeAlgebra

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.superCommuteF_ofCrAnListF_ofCrAnListF
declarations.statement:
lemma superCommuteF_ofCrAnListF_ofCrAnListF (φs φs' : List 𝓕.CrAnFieldOp) :
    [ofCrAnListF φs, ofCrAnListF φs']ₛF =
    ofCrAnListF (φs ++ φs') - 𝓢(𝓕 |>ₛ φs, 𝓕 |>ₛ φs') • ofCrAnListF (φs' ++ φs)

    𝓢(𝓕 |>ₛ φ, 𝓕 |>ₛ φ') • crPartF φ' * crPartF φ +
    [crPartF φ, crPartF φ']ₛF

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.anPartF_mul_anPartF_eq_superCommuteF
declarations.statement:
lemma anPartF_mul_anPartF_eq_superCommuteF (φ φ' : 𝓕.FieldOp) :
    anPartF φ * anPartF φ' = 𝓢(𝓕 |>ₛ φ, 𝓕 |>ₛ φ') • anPartF φ' * anPartF φ +
    [anPartF φ, anPartF φ']ₛF

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.ofCrAnListF_mul_ofFieldOpListF_eq_superCommuteF
declarations.statement:
lemma ofCrAnListF_mul_ofFieldOpListF_eq_superCommuteF (φs : List 𝓕.CrAnFieldOp)
    (φs' : List 𝓕.FieldOp) : ofCrAnListF φs * ofFieldOpListF φs' =
    𝓢(𝓕 |>ₛ φs, 𝓕 |>ₛ φs') • ofFieldOpListF φs' * ofCrAnListF φs
    + [ofCrAnListF φs, ofFieldOpListF φs']ₛF

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.superCommuteF_ofCrAnListF_ofCrAnListF_symm
declarations.statement:
lemma superCommuteF_ofCrAnListF_ofCrAnListF_symm (φs φs' : List 𝓕.CrAnFieldOp) :
    [ofCrAnListF φs, ofCrAnListF φs']ₛF =
    (- 𝓢(𝓕 |>ₛ φs, 𝓕 |>ₛ φs')) • [ofCrAnListF φs', ofCrAnListF φs]ₛF

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.superCommuteF_ofCrAnOpF_ofCrAnOpF_symm
declarations.statement:
lemma superCommuteF_ofCrAnOpF_ofCrAnOpF_symm (φ φ' : 𝓕.CrAnFieldOp) :
    [ofCrAnOpF φ, ofCrAnOpF φ']ₛF =
    (- 𝓢(𝓕 |>ₛ φ, 𝓕 |>ₛ φ')) • [ofCrAnOpF φ', ofCrAnOpF φ]ₛF

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.superCommuteF_ofCrAnListF_ofCrAnListF_cons
declarations.statement:
lemma superCommuteF_ofCrAnListF_ofCrAnListF_cons (φ : 𝓕.CrAnFieldOp) (φs φs' : List 𝓕.CrAnFieldOp) :
    [ofCrAnListF φs, ofCrAnListF (φ :: φs')]ₛF =
    [ofCrAnListF φs, ofCrAnOpF φ]ₛF * ofCrAnListF φs' +
    𝓢(𝓕 |>ₛ φs, 𝓕 |>ₛ φ)
    • ofCrAnOpF φ * [ofCrAnListF φs, ofCrAnListF φs']ₛF

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.superCommuteF_ofCrAnListF_ofFieldOpListF_cons
declarations.statement:
lemma superCommuteF_ofCrAnListF_ofFieldOpListF_cons (φ : 𝓕.FieldOp) (φs : List 𝓕.CrAnFieldOp)
    (φs' : List 𝓕.FieldOp) : [ofCrAnListF φs, ofFieldOpListF (φ :: φs')]ₛF =
    [ofCrAnListF φs, ofFieldOpF φ]ₛF * ofFieldOpListF φs' +
    𝓢(𝓕 |>ₛ φs, 𝓕 |>ₛ φ) • ofFieldOpF φ * [ofCrAnListF φs, ofFieldOpListF φs']ₛF

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.superCommuteF_ofCrAnListF_ofCrAnListF_eq_sum
declarations.doc:
For a field specification `𝓕`, and two lists `φs = φ₀…φₙ` and `φs'` of `𝓕.CrAnFieldOp`
the following super commutation relation holds:

`[φs', φ₀…φₙ]ₛF = ∑ i, 𝓢(φs', φ₀…φᵢ₋₁) • φ₀…φᵢ₋₁ * [φs', φᵢ]ₛF * φᵢ₊₁ … φₙ`

The proof of this relation is via induction on the length of `φs`.
declarations.statement:
lemma superCommuteF_ofCrAnListF_ofCrAnListF_eq_sum (φs : List 𝓕.CrAnFieldOp) :
    (φs' : List 𝓕.CrAnFieldOp) → [ofCrAnListF φs, ofCrAnListF φs']ₛF =
    ∑ (n : Fin φs'.length), 𝓢(𝓕 |>ₛ φs, 𝓕 |>ₛ φs'.take n) •
    ofCrAnListF (φs'.take n) * [ofCrAnListF φs, ofCrAnOpF (φs'.get n)]ₛF *
    ofCrAnListF (φs'.drop (n + 1))

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.superCommuteF_ofCrAnListF_ofFieldOpListF_eq_sum
declarations.statement:
lemma superCommuteF_ofCrAnListF_ofFieldOpListF_eq_sum (φs : List 𝓕.CrAnFieldOp) :
    (φs' : List 𝓕.FieldOp) →
    [ofCrAnListF φs, ofFieldOpListF φs']ₛF =
    ∑ (n : Fin φs'.length), 𝓢(𝓕 |>ₛ φs, 𝓕 |>ₛ φs'.take n) •
      ofFieldOpListF (φs'.take n) * [ofCrAnListF φs, ofFieldOpF (φs'.get n)]ₛF *
      ofFieldOpListF (φs'.drop (n + 1))

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.summerCommute_jacobi_ofCrAnListF
declarations.statement:
lemma summerCommute_jacobi_ofCrAnListF (φs1 φs2 φs3 : List 𝓕.CrAnFieldOp) :
    [ofCrAnListF φs1, [ofCrAnListF φs2, ofCrAnListF φs3]ₛF]ₛF =
    𝓢(𝓕 |>ₛ φs1, 𝓕 |>ₛ φs3) •
    (- 𝓢(𝓕 |>ₛ φs2, 𝓕 |>ₛ φs3) • [ofCrAnListF φs3, [ofCrAnListF φs1, ofCrAnListF φs2]ₛF]ₛF -
    𝓢(𝓕 |>ₛ φs1, 𝓕 |>ₛ φs2) • [ofCrAnListF φs2, [ofCrAnListF φs3, ofCrAnListF φs1]ₛF]ₛF)

    [ofCrAnListF φs, ofCrAnListF φs']ₛF ∈ statisticSubmodule fermionic

    [ofCrAnOpF φ, ofCrAnOpF φ']ₛF ∈ statisticSubmodule fermionic

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.superCommuteF_superCommuteF_ofCrAnOpF_bosonic_or_fermionic
declarations.statement:
lemma superCommuteF_superCommuteF_ofCrAnOpF_bosonic_or_fermionic (φ1 φ2 φ3 : 𝓕.CrAnFieldOp) :

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.superCommuteF_bosonic_ofCrAnListF_eq_sum
declarations.statement:
lemma superCommuteF_bosonic_ofCrAnListF_eq_sum (a : 𝓕.FieldOpFreeAlgebra) (φs : List 𝓕.CrAnFieldOp)
    (ha : a ∈ statisticSubmodule bosonic) :
    [a, ofCrAnListF φs]ₛF = ∑ (n : Fin φs.length),
      ofCrAnListF (φs.take n) * [a, ofCrAnOpF (φs.get n)]ₛF *
      ofCrAnListF (φs.drop (n + 1))

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.superCommuteF_fermionic_ofCrAnListF_eq_sum
declarations.statement:
lemma superCommuteF_fermionic_ofCrAnListF_eq_sum (a : 𝓕.FieldOpFreeAlgebra)
    (φs : List 𝓕.CrAnFieldOp) (ha : a ∈ statisticSubmodule fermionic) :
    [a, ofCrAnListF φs]ₛF = ∑ (n : Fin φs.length), 𝓢(fermionic, 𝓕 |>ₛ φs.take n) •
      ofCrAnListF (φs.take n) * [a, ofCrAnOpF (φs.get n)]ₛF *
      ofCrAnListF (φs.drop (n + 1))

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.timeOrderF
declarations.doc:
For a field specification `𝓕`, `timeOrderF` is the linear map

`FieldOpFreeAlgebra 𝓕 →ₗ[ℂ] FieldOpFreeAlgebra 𝓕`

defined by its action on the basis `ofCrAnListF φs`, taking
`ofCrAnListF φs` to

`crAnTimeOrderSign φs • ofCrAnListF (crAnTimeOrderList φs)`.

That is, `timeOrderF` time-orders the field operators and multiplies by the sign of the
time order.

The notation `𝓣ᶠ(a)` is used for `timeOrderF a`
declarations.statement: def timeOrderF : FieldOpFreeAlgebra 𝓕 →ₗ[ℂ] FieldOpFreeAlgebra 𝓕

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.timeOrderF_ofCrAnListF
declarations.statement:
lemma timeOrderF_ofCrAnListF (φs : List 𝓕.CrAnFieldOp) :
    𝓣ᶠ(ofCrAnListF φs) = crAnTimeOrderSign φs • ofCrAnListF (crAnTimeOrderList φs)

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.timeOrderF_timeOrderF_mid
declarations.statement:
lemma timeOrderF_timeOrderF_mid (a b c : 𝓕.FieldOpFreeAlgebra) :
    𝓣ᶠ(a * b * c) = 𝓣ᶠ(a * 𝓣ᶠ(b) * c)

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.timeOrderF_timeOrderF_right
declarations.statement: lemma timeOrderF_timeOrderF_right (a b : 𝓕.FieldOpFreeAlgebra) : 𝓣ᶠ(a * b) = 𝓣ᶠ(a * 𝓣ᶠ(b))

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.timeOrderF_timeOrderF_left
declarations.statement: lemma timeOrderF_timeOrderF_left (a b : 𝓕.FieldOpFreeAlgebra) : 𝓣ᶠ(a * b) = 𝓣ᶠ(𝓣ᶠ(a) * b)

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.timeOrderF_ofFieldOpListF
declarations.statement:
lemma timeOrderF_ofFieldOpListF (φs : List 𝓕.FieldOp) :
    𝓣ᶠ(ofFieldOpListF φs) = timeOrderSign φs • ofFieldOpListF (timeOrderList φs)

declarations.statement:
lemma timeOrderF_ofFieldOpListF_singleton (φ : 𝓕.FieldOp) :

    (φ1 φ2 φ3 : 𝓕.CrAnFieldOp) (h : ¬
      (crAnTimeOrderRel φ1 φ2 ∧ crAnTimeOrderRel φ1 φ3 ∧

      crAnTimeOrderRel φ3 φ1 ∧ crAnTimeOrderRel φ3 φ2)) :

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.timeOrderF_superCommuteF_ofCrAnOpF_ofCrAnOpF_eq_time
declarations.statement:
lemma timeOrderF_superCommuteF_ofCrAnOpF_ofCrAnOpF_eq_time
    {φ ψ : 𝓕.CrAnFieldOp} (h1 : crAnTimeOrderRel φ ψ) (h2 : crAnTimeOrderRel ψ φ) :
    𝓣ᶠ([ofCrAnOpF φ, ofCrAnOpF ψ]ₛF) = [ofCrAnOpF φ, ofCrAnOpF ψ]ₛF

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.timeOrderF_eq_maxTimeField_mul
declarations.doc:
In the state algebra time, ordering obeys `T(φ₀φ₁…φₙ) = s * φᵢ * T(φ₀φ₁…φᵢ₋₁φᵢ₊₁…φₙ)`
where `φᵢ` is the state
which has maximum time and `s` is the exchange sign of `φᵢ` and `φ₀φ₁…φᵢ₋₁`.
declarations.statement:
lemma timeOrderF_eq_maxTimeField_mul (φ : 𝓕.FieldOp) (φs : List 𝓕.FieldOp) :
    𝓣ᶠ(ofFieldOpListF (φ :: φs)) =
    𝓢(𝓕 |>ₛ maxTimeField φ φs, 𝓕 |>ₛ (φ :: φs).take (maxTimeFieldPos φ φs)) •
    ofFieldOpF (maxTimeField φ φs) * 𝓣ᶠ(ofFieldOpListF (eraseMaxTimeField φ φs))

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.timeOrderF_eq_maxTimeField_mul_finset
declarations.doc:
In the state algebra time, ordering obeys `T(φ₀φ₁…φₙ) = s * φᵢ * T(φ₀φ₁…φᵢ₋₁φᵢ₊₁…φₙ)`
where `φᵢ` is the state
which has maximum time and `s` is the exchange sign of `φᵢ` and `φ₀φ₁…φᵢ₋₁`.
Here `s` is written using finite sets.
declarations.statement:
lemma timeOrderF_eq_maxTimeField_mul_finset (φ : 𝓕.FieldOp) (φs : List 𝓕.FieldOp) :
    𝓣ᶠ(ofFieldOpListF (φ :: φs)) = 𝓢(𝓕 |>ₛ maxTimeField φ φs, 𝓕 |>ₛ ⟨(eraseMaxTimeField φ φs).get,
      (Finset.filter (fun x =>
        (maxTimeFieldPosFin φ φs).succAbove x < maxTimeFieldPosFin φ φs) Finset.univ)⟩) •
      ofFieldOpF (maxTimeField φ φs) * 𝓣ᶠ(ofFieldOpListF (eraseMaxTimeField φ φs))

modules.title: Field specification
modules.doc:
In this module is the definition of a field specification.
A field specification is a structure consisting of a type of fields and a
the field statistics of each field.

From each field we can create three different types of `FieldOp`.
- Negative asymptotic states.
- Position states.
- Positive asymptotic states.

These states carry the same field statistic as the field they are derived from.

## References

* https://particle.physics.ucdavis.edu/modernsusy/slides/slideimages/spinorfeynrules.pdf.
  [ref: ucdavis_spinorfeynrules]

declarations.name: FieldSpecification
declarations.doc:
The structure `FieldSpecification` is defined to have the following content:
  - A type `Field` whose elements are the constituent fields of the theory.
  - For every field `f` in `Field`, a type `PositionLabel f` whose elements label the different
    position operators associated with the field `f`. For example,
    - For `f` a *real-scalar field*, `PositionLabel f` will have a unique element.
    - For `f` a *complex-scalar field*, `PositionLabel f` will have two elements, one for the field
      operator and one for its conjugate.
    - For `f` a *Dirac fermion*, `PositionLabel f` will have eight elements, one for each Lorentz
      index of the field and its conjugate.
    - For `f` a *Weyl fermion*, `PositionLabel f` will have four elements, one for each Lorentz
      index of the field and its conjugate.
  - For every field `f` in `Field`, a type `AsymptoticLabel f` whose elements label the different
    types of incoming asymptotic field operators associated with the
    field `f` (this also matches the types of outgoing asymptotic field operators).
    For example,
    - For `f` a *real-scalar field*, `AsymptoticLabel f` will have a unique element.
    - For `f` a *complex-scalar field*, `AsymptoticLabel f` will have two elements, one for the
      field operator and one for its conjugate.
    - For `f` a *Dirac fermion*, `AsymptoticLabel f` will have four elements, two for each spin.
    - For `f` a *Weyl fermion*, `AsymptoticLabel f` will have two elements, one for each spin.
  - For each field `f` in `Field`, a field statistic `statistic f` which classifies `f` as either
    `bosonic` or `fermionic`.
declarations.statement:
structure FieldSpecification where
  /-- A type whose elements are the constituent fields of the theory. -/
  Field : Type
  /-- For every field `f` in `Field`, the type `PositionLabel f` has elements that label the
    different position operators associated with the field `f`. -/
  PositionLabel : Field → Type
  /-- For every field `f` in `Field`, the type `AsymptoticLabel f` has elements that label
    the different asymptotic based field operators associated with the field `f`. -/
  AsymptoticLabel : Field → Type
  /-- For every field `f` in `Field`, the field statistic `statistic f` classifies `f` as either
    `bosonic` or `fermionic`. -/
  statistic : Field → FieldStatistic

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.FieldOp
declarations.doc:
For a field specification `𝓕`, the inductive type `𝓕.FieldOp` is defined
  to contain the following elements:
- For every `f` in `𝓕.Field`, element of `e` of `AsymptoticLabel f` and `3`-momentum `p`, an
  element labelled `inAsymp f e p` corresponding to an incoming asymptotic field operator
  of the field `f`, of label `e` (e.g. specifying the spin), and momentum `p`.
- For every `f` in `𝓕.Field`, element of `e` of `PositionLabel f` and space-time position `x`, an
  element labelled `position f e x` corresponding to a position field operator of the field `f`,
  of label `e` (e.g. specifying the Lorentz index), and position `x`.
- For every `f` in `𝓕.Field`, element of `e` of `AsymptoticLabel f` and `3`-momentum `p`, an
  element labelled `outAsymp f e p` corresponding to an outgoing asymptotic field operator of the
  field `f`, of label `e` (e.g. specifying the spin), and momentum `p`.

As an example, if `f` corresponds to a Weyl-fermion field, then
- For `inAsymp f e p`, `e` would correspond to a spin `s`, and `inAsymp f e p` would, once
  represented in the operator algebra,
  be proportional to the creation operator `a(p, s)`.
- `position f e x`, `e` would correspond to a Lorentz index `a`, and `position f e x` would,
  once represented in the operator algebra, be proportional to the operator

  `∑ s, ∫ d³p/(…) (xₐ(p,s) a(p, s) e ^ (-i p x) + yₐ(p,s) a†(p, s) e ^ (-i p x))`.

- `outAsymp f e p`, `e` would correspond to a spin `s`, and `outAsymp f e p` would,
  once represented in the operator algebra, be proportional to the
  annihilation operator `a†(p, s)`.
declarations.statement:
inductive FieldOp (𝓕 : FieldSpecification) where
  | inAsymp : (Σ f, 𝓕.AsymptoticLabel f) × (Momentum 3) → 𝓕.FieldOp
  | position : (Σ f, 𝓕.PositionLabel f) × SpaceTime → 𝓕.FieldOp
  | outAsymp : (Σ f, 𝓕.AsymptoticLabel f) × (Momentum 3) → 𝓕.FieldOp

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.statesIsPosition
declarations.doc: The bool on `FieldOp` which is true only for position field operator.
declarations.statement: def statesIsPosition : 𝓕.FieldOp → Bool

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.fieldOpToField
declarations.doc:
For a field specification `𝓕`, `𝓕.fieldOpToField` is defined to take field operators
to their underlying field.
declarations.statement: def fieldOpToField : 𝓕.FieldOp → 𝓕.Field

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.fieldOpStatistic
declarations.doc:
For a field specification `𝓕`, and an element `φ` of `𝓕.FieldOp`.
  The field statistic `fieldOpStatistic φ` is defined to be the statistic associated with
  the field underlying `φ`.

  The following notation is used in relation to `fieldOpStatistic`:
- For `φ` an element of `𝓕.FieldOp`, `𝓕 |>ₛ φ` is `fieldOpStatistic φ`.
- For `φs` a list of `𝓕.FieldOp`, `𝓕 |>ₛ φs` is the product of `fieldOpStatistic φ` over
  the list `φs`.
- For a function `f : Fin n → 𝓕.FieldOp` and a finite set `a` of `Fin n`, `𝓕 |>ₛ ⟨f, a⟩` is the
  product of `fieldOpStatistic (f i)` for all `i ∈ a`.
declarations.statement: def fieldOpStatistic : 𝓕.FieldOp → FieldStatistic

modules.title: Creation and annihilation states
modules.doc:
Called `CrAnFieldOp` for short here.

Given a field specification, in addition to defining states
(see: `Physlib.QFT.PerturbationTheory.FieldSpecification.Basic`),
we can also define creation and annihilation states.
These are similar to states but come with an additional specification of whether they correspond to
creation or annihilation operators.

In particular we have the following creation and annihilation states for each field:
- Negative asymptotic states - with the implicit specification that it is a creation state.
- Position states with a creation specification.
- Position states with an annihilation specification.
- Positive asymptotic states - with the implicit specification that it is an annihilation state.

In this module in addition to defining `CrAnFieldOp` we also define some maps:
- The map `crAnFieldOpToFieldOp` takes a `CrAnFieldOp` to its state in `FieldOp`.
- The map `crAnFieldOpToCreateAnnihilate` takes a `CrAnFieldOp` to its corresponding
`CreateAnnihilate` value.
- The map `crAnStatistics` takes a `CrAnFieldOp` to its corresponding `FieldStatistic`
(bosonic or fermionic).

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.fieldOpToCrAnType
declarations.doc:
To each field operator the specification of the type of creation and annihilation parts.
For asymptotic states there is only one allowed part, whilst for position
field operator there is two.
declarations.statement: def fieldOpToCrAnType : 𝓕.FieldOp → Type

declarations.doc: The instance of a finite type on `𝓕.fieldOpToCreateAnnihilateType i`.
declarations.statement: instance : ∀ i, Fintype (𝓕.fieldOpToCrAnType i)

declarations.doc: The instance of a decidable equality on `𝓕.fieldOpToCreateAnnihilateType i`.
declarations.statement: instance : ∀ i, DecidableEq (𝓕.fieldOpToCrAnType i)

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.fieldOpToCreateAnnihilateTypeCongr
declarations.doc:
The equivalence between `𝓕.fieldOpToCreateAnnihilateType i` and
`𝓕.fieldOpToCreateAnnihilateType j` from an equality `i = j`.
declarations.statement:
def fieldOpToCreateAnnihilateTypeCongr : {i j : 𝓕.FieldOp} → i = j →
    𝓕.fieldOpToCrAnType i ≃ 𝓕.fieldOpToCrAnType j

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.CrAnFieldOp
declarations.doc:
For a field specification `𝓕`, the (sigma) type `𝓕.CrAnFieldOp`
corresponds to the type of creation and annihilation parts of field operators.
It formally defined to consist of the following elements:
- For each incoming asymptotic field operator `φ` in `𝓕.FieldOp` an element
  written as `⟨φ, ()⟩` in `𝓕.CrAnFieldOp`, corresponding to the creation part of `φ`.
  Here `φ` has no annihilation part. (Here `()` is the unique element of `Unit`.)
- For each position field operator `φ` in `𝓕.FieldOp` an element of `𝓕.CrAnFieldOp`
  written as `⟨φ, .create⟩`, corresponding to the creation part of `φ`.
- For each position field operator `φ` in `𝓕.FieldOp` an element of `𝓕.CrAnFieldOp`
  written as `⟨φ, .annihilate⟩`, corresponding to the annihilation part of `φ`.
- For each outgoing asymptotic field operator `φ` in `𝓕.FieldOp` an element
  written as `⟨φ, ()⟩` in `𝓕.CrAnFieldOp`, corresponding to the annihilation part of `φ`.
  Here `φ` has no creation part. (Here `()` is the unique element of `Unit`.)

As an example, if `f` corresponds to a Weyl-fermion field, it would contribute
  the following elements to `𝓕.CrAnFieldOp`
- For each spin `s`, an element corresponding to an incoming asymptotic operator: `a(p, s)`.
- For each each Lorentz
  index `a`, an element corresponding to the creation part of a position operator:

  `∑ s, ∫ d³p/(…) (xₐ (p,s) a(p, s) e ^ (-i p x))`.
- For each each Lorentz
  index `a`,an element corresponding to annihilation part of a position operator:

  `∑ s, ∫ d³p/(…) (yₐ(p,s) a†(p, s) e ^ (-i p x))`.
- For each spin `s`, element corresponding to an outgoing asymptotic operator: `a†(p, s)`.
declarations.statement: def CrAnFieldOp : Type

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.crAnFieldOpToFieldOp
declarations.doc: The map from creation and annihilation field operator to their underlying states.
declarations.statement: def crAnFieldOpToFieldOp : 𝓕.CrAnFieldOp → 𝓕.FieldOp

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.crAnFieldOpToFieldOp_prod
declarations.statement:
lemma crAnFieldOpToFieldOp_prod (s : 𝓕.FieldOp) (t : 𝓕.fieldOpToCrAnType s) :
    𝓕.crAnFieldOpToFieldOp ⟨s, t⟩ = s

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.crAnFieldOpToCreateAnnihilate
declarations.doc:
For a field specification `𝓕`, `𝓕.crAnFieldOpToCreateAnnihilate` is the map from
  `𝓕.CrAnFieldOp` to `CreateAnnihilate` taking `φ` to `create` if
- `φ` corresponds to an incoming asymptotic field operator or the creation part of a position based
  field operator.

otherwise it takes `φ` to `annihilate`.
declarations.statement: def crAnFieldOpToCreateAnnihilate : 𝓕.CrAnFieldOp → CreateAnnihilate

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.crAnStatistics
declarations.doc:
For a field specification `𝓕`, and an element `φ` in `𝓕.CrAnFieldOp`, the field
statistic `crAnStatistics φ` is defined to be the statistic associated with the field `𝓕.Field`
(or the `𝓕.FieldOp`) underlying `φ`.

The following notation is used in relation to `crAnStatistics`:
- For `φ` an element of `𝓕.CrAnFieldOp`, `𝓕 |>ₛ φ` is `crAnStatistics φ`.
- For `φs` a list of `𝓕.CrAnFieldOp`, `𝓕 |>ₛ φs` is the product of `crAnStatistics φ` over
  the list `φs`.
declarations.statement: def crAnStatistics : 𝓕.CrAnFieldOp → FieldStatistic

modules.title: Creation and annihilation sections
modules.doc:
In the module
`Physlib.QFT.PerturbationTheory.FieldSpecification.Basic`
we defined states for a field specification, and in the module
`Physlib.QFT.PerturbationTheory.FieldStatistics.CrAnFieldOp`
we defined a refinement of states called `CrAnFieldOp` which distinguishes between the
creation and annihilation components of states.
There exists, in particular, a map from `CrAnFieldOp` to `FieldOp` called `crAnFieldOpToFieldOp`.

Given a list of `FieldOp`, `φs`, in this module we define a section of `φs` to be a list of
`CrAnFieldOp`, `ψs`, such that under the map `crAnFieldOpToFieldOp`, `ψs` is mapped to `φs`.
That is to say, the states underlying `ψs` are the states in `φs`.
We denote these sections as `CrAnSection φs`.

Looking forward the main consequence of this definition is the lemma
`FieldSpecification.FieldOpFreeAlgebra.ofFieldOpListF_sum`.

In this module we define various properties of `CrAnSection`.

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.CrAnSection
declarations.doc:
The sections in `𝓕.CrAnFieldOp` over a list `φs : List 𝓕.FieldOp`.
In terms of physics, given some fields `φ₁...φₙ`, the different ways one can associate
each field as a `creation` or an `annilation` operator. E.g. the number of terms
`φ₁⁰φ₂¹...φₙ⁰` `φ₁¹φ₂¹...φₙ⁰` etc. If some fields are exclusively creation or annihilation
operators at this point (e.g. asymptotic states) this is accounted for.
declarations.statement: def CrAnSection (φs : List 𝓕.FieldOp) : Type

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.CrAnSection.length_eq
declarations.statement: lemma length_eq (ψs : CrAnSection φs) : ψs.1.length = φs.length

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.CrAnSection.tail
declarations.doc: The tail of a section for `φs`.
declarations.statement: def tail : {φs : List 𝓕.FieldOp} → (ψs : CrAnSection φs) → CrAnSection φs.tail

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.CrAnSection.head_state_eq
declarations.statement:
lemma head_state_eq {φ : 𝓕.FieldOp} : (ψs : CrAnSection (φ :: φs)) →
    (ψs.1.head (by simp [← List.length_pos_iff_ne_nil])).1 = φ

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.CrAnSection.statistics_eq_state_statistics
declarations.statement:
lemma statistics_eq_state_statistics (ψs : CrAnSection φs) :
    (𝓕 |>ₛ ψs.1) = 𝓕 |>ₛ φs

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.CrAnSection.take_statistics_eq_take_state_statistics
declarations.statement:
lemma take_statistics_eq_take_state_statistics (ψs : CrAnSection φs) n :
    (𝓕 |>ₛ (ψs.1.take n)) = 𝓕 |>ₛ (φs.take n)

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.CrAnSection.head
declarations.doc: The head of a section for `φ :: φs` as an element in `𝓕.fieldOpToCreateAnnihilateType φ`.
declarations.statement:
def head : {φ : 𝓕.FieldOp} → (ψs : CrAnSection (φ :: φs)) →
    𝓕.fieldOpToCrAnType φ

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.CrAnSection.eq_head_cons_tail
declarations.statement:
lemma eq_head_cons_tail {φ : 𝓕.FieldOp} {ψs : CrAnSection (φ :: φs)} :
    ψs.1 = ⟨φ, head ψs⟩ :: ψs.tail.1

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.CrAnSection.cons
declarations.doc:
The creation of a section from for `φ : φs` from a section for `φs` and a
element of `𝓕.fieldOpToCreateAnnihilateType φ`.
declarations.statement:
def cons {φ : 𝓕.FieldOp} (ψ : 𝓕.fieldOpToCrAnType φ) (ψs : CrAnSection φs) :
    CrAnSection (φ :: φs)

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.CrAnSection.nilEquiv
declarations.doc:
For the empty list of states there is only one `CrAnSection`. Corresponding to the
empty list of `CrAnFieldOp`.
declarations.statement: def nilEquiv : CrAnSection (𝓕 := 𝓕) [] ≃ Unit

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.CrAnSection.singletonEquiv
declarations.doc:
The creation and annihilation sections for a singleton list is given by
a choice of `𝓕.fieldOpToCreateAnnihilateType φ`. If `φ` is a asymptotic state
there is no choice here, else there are two choices.
declarations.statement:
def singletonEquiv {φ : 𝓕.FieldOp} : CrAnSection [φ] ≃
    𝓕.fieldOpToCrAnType φ

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.CrAnSection.consEquiv
declarations.doc:
An equivalence separating the head of a creation and annihilation section
from the tail.
declarations.statement:
def consEquiv {φ : 𝓕.FieldOp} {φs : List 𝓕.FieldOp} : CrAnSection (φ :: φs) ≃
    𝓕.fieldOpToCrAnType φ × CrAnSection φs

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.CrAnSection.fintype
declarations.doc:
The instance of a finite type on `CrAnSection`s defined recursively through
`consEquiv`.
declarations.statement: instance fintype : (φs : List 𝓕.FieldOp) → Fintype (CrAnSection φs)

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.CrAnSection.card_nil_eq
declarations.statement: lemma card_nil_eq : Fintype.card (CrAnSection (𝓕 := 𝓕) []) = 1

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.CrAnSection.card_cons_eq
declarations.statement:
lemma card_cons_eq {φ : 𝓕.FieldOp} {φs : List 𝓕.FieldOp} :
    Fintype.card (CrAnSection (φ :: φs)) = Fintype.card (𝓕.fieldOpToCrAnType φ) *
    Fintype.card (CrAnSection φs)

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.CrAnSection.card_eq_mul
declarations.statement:
lemma card_eq_mul : {φs : List 𝓕.FieldOp} → Fintype.card (CrAnSection φs) =
    2 ^ (List.countP 𝓕.statesIsPosition φs)

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.CrAnSection.card_perm_eq
declarations.statement:
lemma card_perm_eq {φs φs' : List 𝓕.FieldOp} (h : φs.Perm φs') :
    Fintype.card (CrAnSection φs) = Fintype.card (CrAnSection φs')

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.CrAnSection.sum_nil
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_nil (f : CrAnSection (𝓕 := 𝓕) [] → M) [AddCommMonoid M] :
    ∑ (s : CrAnSection []), f s = f ⟨[], rfl⟩

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.CrAnSection.sum_cons
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_cons (f : CrAnSection (φ :: φs) → M) [AddCommMonoid M] :
    ∑ (s : CrAnSection (φ :: φs)), f s = ∑ (a : 𝓕.fieldOpToCrAnType φ),
    ∑ (s : CrAnSection φs), f (cons a s)

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.CrAnSection.sum_over_length
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_over_length {s : CrAnSection φs} (f : Fin s.1.length → M)
    [AddCommMonoid M] : ∑ (n : Fin s.1.length), f n =
    ∑ (n : Fin φs.length), f (Fin.cast (length_eq s).symm n)

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.CrAnSection.congr
declarations.doc:
The equivalence between `CrAnSection φs` and
`CrAnSection φs'` induced by an equality `φs = φs'`.
declarations.statement:
def congr : {φs φs' : List 𝓕.FieldOp} → (h : φs = φs') →
    CrAnSection φs ≃ CrAnSection φs'

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.CrAnSection.congr_fst
declarations.statement:
lemma congr_fst {φs φs' : List 𝓕.FieldOp} (h : φs = φs') (ψs : CrAnSection φs) :
    (congr h ψs).1 = ψs.1

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.CrAnSection.congr_symm
declarations.statement:
lemma congr_symm {φs φs' : List 𝓕.FieldOp} (h : φs = φs') :
    (congr h).symm = congr h.symm

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.CrAnSection.congr_trans_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma congr_trans_apply {φs φs' φs'' : List 𝓕.FieldOp} (h1 : φs = φs') (h2 : φs' = φs'')
    (ψs : CrAnSection φs) :
    (congr h2 (congr h1 ψs)) = congr (by rw [h1, h2]) ψs

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.CrAnSection.take
declarations.doc: Returns the first `n` elements of a section and its underlying list.
declarations.statement: def take (n : ℕ) (ψs : CrAnSection φs) : CrAnSection (φs.take n)

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.CrAnSection.take_congr
declarations.statement:
lemma take_congr {φs φs' : List 𝓕.FieldOp} (h : φs = φs') (n : ℕ)
    (ψs : CrAnSection φs) :
    (take n (congr h ψs)) = congr (by rw [h]) (take n ψs)

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.CrAnSection.drop
declarations.doc: Removes the first `n` elements of a section and its underlying list.
declarations.statement: def drop (n : ℕ) (ψs : CrAnSection φs) : CrAnSection (φs.drop n)

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.CrAnSection.drop_congr
declarations.statement:
lemma drop_congr {φs φs' : List 𝓕.FieldOp} (h : φs = φs') (n : ℕ)
    (ψs : CrAnSection φs) :
    (drop n (congr h ψs)) = congr (by rw [h]) (drop n ψs)

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.CrAnSection.append
declarations.doc: Appends two sections and their underlying lists.
declarations.statement:
def append {φs φs' : List 𝓕.FieldOp} (ψs : CrAnSection φs)
    (ψs' : CrAnSection φs') : CrAnSection (φs ++ φs')

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.CrAnSection.append_assoc
declarations.statement:
lemma append_assoc {φs φs' φs'' : List 𝓕.FieldOp} (ψs : CrAnSection φs)
    (ψs' : CrAnSection φs') (ψs'' : CrAnSection φs'') :
    append ψs (append ψs' ψs'') = congr (by simp) (append (append ψs ψs') ψs'')

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.CrAnSection.append_assoc'
declarations.statement:
lemma append_assoc' {φs φs' φs'' : List 𝓕.FieldOp} (ψs : CrAnSection φs)
    (ψs' : CrAnSection φs') (ψs'' : CrAnSection φs'') :
    (append (append ψs ψs') ψs'') = congr (by simp) (append ψs (append ψs' ψs''))

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.CrAnSection.singletonEquiv_append_eq_cons
FieldSpecification.CrAnSection.take_append_drop
declarations.statement:
lemma take_append_drop {n : ℕ} (ψs : CrAnSection φs) :
    append (take n ψs) (drop n ψs) = congr (List.take_append_drop n φs).symm ψs

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.CrAnSection.congr_append
declarations.statement:
lemma congr_append {φs1 φs1' φs2 φs2' : List 𝓕.FieldOp} (h1 : φs1 = φs1') (h2 : φs2 = φs2')
    (ψs1 : CrAnSection φs1) (ψs2 : CrAnSection φs2) :
    (append (congr h1 ψs1) (congr h2 ψs2)) = congr (by rw [h1, h2]) (append ψs1 ψs2)

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.CrAnSection.congr_fst_append
declarations.statement:
lemma congr_fst_append {φs1 φs1' φs2 : List 𝓕.FieldOp} (h1 : φs1 = φs1')
    (ψs1 : CrAnSection φs1) (ψs2 : CrAnSection φs2) :
    (append (congr h1 ψs1) (ψs2)) = congr (by rw [h1]) (append ψs1 ψs2)

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.CrAnSection.congr_snd_append
declarations.statement:
lemma congr_snd_append {φs1 φs2 φs2' : List 𝓕.FieldOp} (h2 : φs2 = φs2')
    (ψs1 : CrAnSection φs1) (ψs2 : CrAnSection φs2) :
    (append ψs1 (congr h2 ψs2)) = congr (by rw [h2]) (append ψs1 ψs2)

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.CrAnSection.take_left
declarations.statement:
lemma take_left {φs φs' : List 𝓕.FieldOp} (ψs : CrAnSection φs)
    (ψs' : CrAnSection φs') :
    take φs.length (ψs.append ψs') = congr (by simp) ψs

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.CrAnSection.drop_left
declarations.statement:
lemma drop_left {φs φs' : List 𝓕.FieldOp} (ψs : CrAnSection φs)
    (ψs' : CrAnSection φs') :
    drop φs.length (ψs.append ψs') = congr (by simp) ψs'

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.CrAnSection.appendEquiv
declarations.doc:
The equivalence between `CrAnSection (φs ++ φs')` and
`CrAnSection φs × CrAnSection φs` formed by `append`, `take`
and `drop` and their interrelationship.
declarations.statement:
def appendEquiv {φs φs' : List 𝓕.FieldOp} : CrAnSection (φs ++ φs') ≃
    CrAnSection φs × CrAnSection φs'

declarations.name: List.map_eraseIdx
declarations.statement:
lemma _root_.List.map_eraseIdx {α β : Type} (f : α → β) : (l : List α) → (n : ℕ) →
    List.map f (l.eraseIdx n) = (List.map f l).eraseIdx n

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.CrAnSection.eraseIdx
declarations.doc: Erasing an element from a section and it's underlying list.
declarations.statement: def eraseIdx (n : ℕ) (ψs : CrAnSection φs) : CrAnSection (φs.eraseIdx n)

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.CrAnSection.eraseIdxEquiv
declarations.doc: The equivalence formed by extracting an element from a section.

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.CrAnSection.eraseIdxEquiv_apply_snd
declarations.statement:
lemma eraseIdxEquiv_apply_snd {n : ℕ} (ψs : CrAnSection φs) (hn : n < φs.length) :
    (eraseIdxEquiv n φs hn ψs).snd = eraseIdx n ψs

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.CrAnSection.eraseIdxEquiv_symm_eq_take_cons_drop
declarations.statement:
lemma eraseIdxEquiv_symm_eq_take_cons_drop {n : ℕ} (φs : List 𝓕.FieldOp) (hn : n < φs.length)
    (a : 𝓕.fieldOpToCrAnType φs[n]) (s : CrAnSection (φs.eraseIdx n)) :
    (eraseIdxEquiv n φs hn).symm ⟨a, s⟩ =
    congr (by
    rw [Physlib.List.take_eraseIdx_same, Physlib.List.drop_eraseIdx_succ]
    conv_rhs => rw [← List.take_append_drop n φs]) (append (take n s) (cons a (drop n s)))

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.CrAnSection.eraseIdxEquiv_symm_getElem
declarations.statement:
lemma eraseIdxEquiv_symm_getElem {n : ℕ} (φs : List 𝓕.FieldOp) (hn : n < φs.length)
    (a : 𝓕.fieldOpToCrAnType φs[n]) (s : CrAnSection (φs.eraseIdx n)) :
    getElem ((eraseIdxEquiv n φs hn).symm ⟨a,s⟩).1 n
    (by rw [length_eq]; exact hn) = ⟨φs[n], a⟩

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.CrAnSection.eraseIdxEquiv_symm_eraseIdx
declarations.statement:
lemma eraseIdxEquiv_symm_eraseIdx {n : ℕ} (φs : List 𝓕.FieldOp) (hn : n < φs.length)
    (a : 𝓕.fieldOpToCrAnType φs[n]) (s : CrAnSection (φs.eraseIdx n)) :
    ((eraseIdxEquiv n φs hn).symm ⟨a, s⟩).1.eraseIdx n = s.1

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.CrAnSection.sum_eraseIdxEquiv
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_eraseIdxEquiv (n : ℕ) (φs : List 𝓕.FieldOp) (hn : n < φs.length)
    (f : CrAnSection φs → M) [AddCommMonoid M] : ∑ (s : CrAnSection φs), f s =
    ∑ (a : 𝓕.fieldOpToCrAnType φs[n]), ∑ (s : CrAnSection (φs.eraseIdx n)),
    f ((eraseIdxEquiv n φs hn).symm ⟨a, s⟩)

declarations.name: FieldSpecification.createFilter
declarations.doc:
Given a list of creation and annihilation states, the filtered list only containing
